memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then he ran to the herd and selected a choice, tender calf and gave it to a servant, who hurried to prepare it. He then brought some curds and milk and the calf that had been prepared, and set these before them. While they ate, he stood near them under a tree. - Gen 18:7-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a picture of humble service. Abraham - wealthy, elderly, the honoured head of a large household - runs to the herd himself, selects the best calf, and personally sets the meal before his guests. And then, astonishingly, "he stood near them" while they ate, ready to serve, like a waiter attending his guests. The great patriarch waits on strangers.

This is deeply counter-cultural. Abraham had servants who could have done all this. He could have sat down as an equal, or even had the guests wait on him. Instead, he chooses the posture of a servant, personally attending to their needs. Greatness, in God's eyes, stoops to serve.

Notice too that he gave his best - "a choice, tender calf," not the leftovers or the second-rate. When we truly serve others, we give them our best, not our scraps. Half-hearted service that offers the least we can get away with is not the service God honours.

This humble, serving heart points us straight to Jesus, who "did not come to be served, but to serve" (Matt 20:28), and who took a towel and washed His disciples' feet (John 13:4-5). The Lord of glory stooped lower than Abraham ever did. When we serve others with our own hands, giving our best, we walk in the footsteps of our serving Saviour.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Are you willing to serve others with your own hands, giving your best?
- Where might God be calling you to take the humble posture of a servant?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You came not to be served but to serve, stooping even to wash feet. Give me a heart like that - willing to serve others humbly, with my own hands, offering my best rather than my scraps.
Amen.
